entries.subject: LAM 2021 216_Kleopatra_mpcd.obj
entries.finding: LAM 2021 `216_Kleopatra_mpcd.obj` — Released detailed shape with both lobes and concave neck — Included. Original 1,586 vertices and 3,168 faces in km. The numerical volume is 865,179.55 km³, matching the MPCD paper's nominal 865,000 km³. The release has 3,168 faces whereas the paper describes 3,136; that difference is recorded rather than editing the source.

entries.subject: LAM 216_Kleopatra_adam.obj
entries.finding: LAM `216_Kleopatra_adam.obj` — Independent reconstruction in the same survey — Downloaded and surveyed as a geometry comparison. Excluded as a duplicate presentation; MPCD better fits the SPHERE images in the source paper.

entries.subject: Shepard et al. 2018 radar revision
entries.finding: [Shepard et al. 2018 radar revision](https://echo.jpl.nasa.gov/asteroids/shepard.etal.2018.kleopatra.pdf) — Updated Arecibo and occultation model; a longer body than the old PDS model — Surveyed through the newer paper's direct shape comparison. Superseded here by the SPHERE-constrained model. No radar albedo is interpreted as an optical texture.

entries.subject: LAM reduced/deconvolved SPHERE images and CDS J/A+A/653/A57
entries.finding: Reopened and adopted. Five deconvolved frames from the 2017 apparition are now the SPHERE photograph lens. The camera is computed, not fitted: pole, period and phase epoch come from the release’s own parameter record, observing geometry from JPL Horizons for Paranal, and plate scale, exposure time and filter from each frame’s own header. The rotation convention is čurech, Sidorin and Kaasalainen (2010) equation 1. Predicted limb position angles match the observed half-maximum contour to 3.3 degrees root mean square over seven frames spanning both apparitions, with no free parameter; predicted disc sizes agree with the archived angular diameter to under two percent. The paper’s caution that inferred albedo features near the limb may originate in deconvolution artefacts still stands, which is why the lens states photographed illumination and matched relative brightness rather than albedo.

entries.subject: Older DAMIT geometry and phase as a replacement
entries.finding: [DAMIT Kleopatra entry](https://astro.troja.mff.cuni.cz/projects/damit/asteroids/view/1044) — 2017 ADAM model and IAU spin data — Live entry inspected. Older geometry/phase are not silently mixed with the 2021 MPCD release.
entries.revisitWhen: An explicit registration and scientific reason to use the older geometry or phase with the selected 2021 MPCD release.

entries.subject: LAM 216_Kleopatra_param.txt
entries.finding: Resolved. The record is the standard light-curve inversion parameter layout: pole latitude, pole longitude and sidereal period on the first line, then the phase epoch and the phase at that epoch. Its column order was established against published poles rather than assumed, because the survey’s files are not consistent: most are latitude first, but at least Pallas, Hygiea, Psyche and Elektra are longitude first, and Elektra’s second value of -92.27 is not a latitude at all. Kleopatra reads latitude first. The convention was then checked against the producer’s own numbers: DAMIT distributes model 101 both as an inversion record and as IAU elements, and converting the first reproduces the second’s pole to under half a degree and its rate to 1e-4 degrees per day. The pole differs slightly from the paper’s printed values because the paper prints separate ADAM and MPCD solutions; this record describes the ADAM frame.

entries.subject: Which reconstruction the rotation parameters describe
entries.finding: The release ships two meshes for this body and one parameter record, and the record describes the ADAM reconstruction rather than the MPCD one that Marchis et al. re-optimised. Measured over seven frames and two apparitions, projecting through the ADAM mesh reproduces the observed limb position angle to 3.3 degrees; the identical parameters through MPCD give 6.8 degrees, and substituting the paper’s printed MPCD pole does not recover it. The photographic lens therefore rides the ADAM mesh while the shape view keeps MPCD, which is the shape-per-dataset pairing the celestial skill requires. Lutetia is a warning for anyone extending this: its MPCD mesh is turned 180 degrees from its ADAM mesh, so one parameter record cannot serve both.

entries.subject: 2018 apparition frames and the level-matching budget
entries.finding: The 2018 apparition views the opposite hemisphere and would roughly double the photographed surface, but its frames cannot be combined with the 2017 set here. Level matching puts the 2017 frames within 0.78 to 1.07 of each other and the two 2018 frames at 0.059 and 0.085, about seventeen times fainter, past this route’s budget of sixteen. Several cross-apparition pairs also share no accepted samples, so that ratio is poorly constrained rather than demonstrated. Both frames stay pinned as registration evidence, since they are what shows the spin solution holding across seventeen months, but they are not lens input.
entries.revisitWhen: The frames are placed on a common photometric scale, by the producers or by a documented per-frame normalisation, or enough overlapping coverage is found to constrain the ratio directly. Raising the matching budget alone would not qualify them.
